title: A patient with sporadic Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease: challenges of rare diseases in the COVID-19 era
case_prompt:
A 76-year-old woman, previously independent, was referred during the COVID-19 pandemic with a 6-week history of cognitive decline. Her daughter reported difficulty navigating her own home and impairment in familiar tasks such as using cutlery. Over this period, she became mood-labile and developed psychotic features, including delusions that her family was poisoning her and visual hallucinations of the room expanding and contracting. 

Her medical history included rheumatic heart disease with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, stage 3B chronic kidney disease, and depression for which sertraline had been started 3 weeks earlier. 

On neurological examination, she was unsteady on her feet and had visual and tactile neglect on the left side. Reflexes were brisk throughout, and she exhibited startle myoclonus. She had an inappropriate affect, giggling in response to questions, and scored 5/10 on the Abbreviated Mental Test. 

Routine blood tests were within normal limits except for an elevated INR of 9.9. She was apyrexial and had no respiratory symptoms. An urgent noncontrast CT scan of the head was performed to exclude subdural haematoma and was unremarkable.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Subdural haematoma was excluded by imaging — “urgent computed tomography head was carried out … and this was unremarkable.”  
2. Alzheimer’s or Lewy body dementia combined with delirium was considered — “Alzheimer’s or Lewy body dementia (combined with delirium, leading to rapid deterioration).”  
3. Limbic encephalitis was considered — “Limbic encephalitis.”  
4. Cerebrovascular disease was considered — “Cerebrovascular disease.”  
5. CNS neoplasm was considered — “CNS neoplasm.”  
6. CNS infection (including COVID-19) was considered — “CNS infection (including COVID-19).”  
7. Systemic infection was considered — “Systemic Infection.”  
8. Electrolyte derangement was considered — “Electrolyte derangement.”  
9. Vitamin deficiency was considered — “Vitamin deficiency.”  
10. Inflammatory conditions were considered — “Inflammatory conditions: vasculitis, sarcoidosis, systemic lupus erythematosus.”  
11. Other systemic disease (hepatic, renal, thyroid) was considered — “Other systemic disease—hepatic, renal, thyroid.”  
12. Sertraline overdose leading to serotonin syndrome was considered — “Sertraline overdose leading to serotonin syndrome.”  
13. Depression was considered — “Depression.”  
14. First-episode psychosis was considered — “First-episode psychosis.”  
15. Sertraline-induced mania was considered — “Sertraline-induced mania.”  
16. Functional disorder was considered — “Functional disorder.”  
17. Sporadic CJD was confirmed by characteristic MRI changes and highly specific CSF assay — “This revealed a cortical ribboning pattern, which was hyperintense on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and FLAIR sequences … suspicious for CJD … Real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) … yields 80% sensitivity and close to 100% specificity for CJD.”
